name: Pakistan
summary_text: Pakistan is dangerous — legally progressive on paper but severely undermined in practice. The 2018 Transgender Persons Protection Act was "one of the most progressive internationally" (third-gender recognition since 2009), but the Federal Shariat Court gutted it in 2023 (declaring provisions "un-Islamic"). Transgender people face extreme violence: three trans women were shot dead in Karachi (bodies on a roadside), 267 violence cases were documented in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and police commit a documented "continuum of violence — from routine harassment to arbitrary detention, extortion, and abuse in custody." The jirga (tribal) system closes cases under family pressure. Same-sex conduct is NOT clearly criminalised nationally (the Zina Ordinance is unclear; no known cases or executions), and there is no Sharia cross-dressing criminalisation (unlike Malaysia). No trans-traveler-specific border friction or death in custody is documented (unlike the UAE or Indonesia). But the severity of social and police violence is extreme. Pakistan has a significant hijra/third-gender community with some legal recognition, and civil society is active (a dedicated ride-sharing service for trans safety launched in Lahore, and activists are appealing the Shariat Court ruling to the Supreme Court).

sources.claim_summary: AP (Nov 2024): 'Shooting kills 3 transgender women in Pakistan's largest city' — gunmen shot three transgender women at close range near Karachi, the second deadly attack on the community there in a week.

sources.title: Bodies of three transgender people found in Pakistan
sources.claim_summary: BBC (Sept 2025): the bodies of three transgender people, shot dead, were found on a roadside in Karachi's Memon Goth area - the latest violence against a community of an estimated half a million trans citizens facing social exclusion and abuse; Amnesty notes a concerning rise in violence; the 2018 Transgender Rights Act's key sections were later revoked by a sharia court.

sources.title: Policy Brief: Preventing Torture Against Transgender Persons in Pakistan - JPP
sources.claim_summary: Justice Project Pakistan policy brief (April 2026): 'Preventing Torture Against Transgender Persons in Pakistan' - trans people face a continuum of violence from law enforcement (harassment, arbitrary detention, extortion, custodial abuse); the challenge is not absence of legal protections but failure of implementation - no binding operational frameworks, independent oversight or accessible complaint mechanisms.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity or expression, Pakistan, November 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office CPIN Pakistan: sexual orientation and gender identity or expression (Nov 2025, updated July 2026): official country-of-origin information and assessment for asylum claims.

sources.title: Pakistan: Revocation of rights of transgender and gender-diverse people must be stopped - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (May 2023): responding to the Federal Shariat Court's reserved verdict striking down sections of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2018 - 'a blow to the rights of the already beleaguered group'; some court observations were based on presumptive scenarios rather than empirical evidence.

sources.title: Between legal rights and lived realities
sources.claim_summary: The News (Oct 2025): 'Between legal rights and lived realities' - despite the 2018 Act, trans Pakistanis face violence, harassment, landlord rejection and hospital/police apathy; in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa alone 267 cases of violence over five years with only one conviction; traces the legal history from the Criminal Tribes Act 1871 through the 2011 Supreme Court recognition, the 2018 Act, the 2020 'X' marker rules, and the 2023 FSC strike-down of self-identification.

sources.title: Anti-trans officials and violence reverse progress for transgender Pakistanis
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Feb 2026): anti-trans officials and violence reverse progress for transgender Pakistanis - Senator Mushtaq Ahmad proposes a government 'gender re-assignment board' controlling official gender identity; a wave of violence (shootings at activists' homes) has left trans people afraid to go out; the 2023 shariat court ruling undercut the 2018 law.

sources.title: Westernised transgenders or colonised transphobes? Examining the FSC verdict on the Transgender Rights Act - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
sources.claim_summary: Dawn (May 2023) by Nayyab Ali: 'Westernised transgenders or colonised transphobes?' - examines the FSC verdict on the Transgender Rights Act; the petitioners' concerns echo right-wing Western anti-trans narratives; describes the 2018 Act's protections (anti-discrimination, welfare, offences against trans people).

sources.title: Pakistan’s Transgender Citizens: Legally Recognized, Socially Forsaken – The Diplomat
sources.claim_summary: The Diplomat (July 2025): Pakistan's transgender citizens - legally recognized, socially forsaken; for 500,000 trans Pakistanis, constitutional rights remain hollow in the face of violence and exclusion.

US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Pakistan: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under Section 377; societal violence and discrimination; transgender persons (khwaja sira) have some legal recognition but face harassment and violence.
